:::{#thm-mixture-mean}
#### The mean of a mixture is the weighted mean of the component means

If $X$ has density ${\p_{\text{mix}}}$ (@def-mixture),
and each component ${\p_c}$ has a defined mean $\mean_c = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x \, {\p_c}(x)\,dx$,
then:

$$\E{X} = \sumto{c}{K} w_c \, \mean_c$$

:::

::: proof

The integral defining $\E{X}$ converges absolutely,
because $\int_{-\infty}^\infty \abs{x} \, {\p_{\text{mix}}}(x)\,dx = \sumto{c}{K} w_c \int_{-\infty}^\infty \abs{x} \, {\p_c}(x)\,dx$,
a finite sum of finite numbers. Then:

$$
\ba
\E{X}
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x \, {\p_{\text{mix}}}(x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of expectation)} \\
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x \sumto{c}{K} w_c \, {\p_c}(x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of a mixture)} \\
&= \sumto{c}{K} w_c \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x \, {\p_c}(x)\,dx
&& \text{(a finite sum of integrals is the integral of the sum)} \\
&= \sumto{c}{K} w_c \, \mean_c
&& \text{(definition of } \mean_c \text{)}
\ea
$$

The first step is the [definition of expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation).

:::
